bidirectional_relay.pipelined_upstream: Bytes consumed with the SOCKS5/HTTP handshake are written once before relay and are included first in the upstream observation; subsequent local bytes follow in wire order.
bidirectional_relay.downstream: Remote bytes continue to drain to the local client after local write EOF. Remote EOF ends downstream delivery.
bidirectional_relay.local_half_close: Local write EOF is a half-close. It ends only local-to-remote copying and must not discard unread local bytes, abort the peer, or close the remote stream before its response is drained.
teardown_order: downstream EOF may half-close the local socket write side
the upstream worker must drain local EOF and finish before the owning socket read side is shut down
full local/remote teardown occurs after both copy directions have quiesced
bidirectional_relay.observation: Emit exactly one observation after both directions finish. Preserve protocol, target, ordered bounded prefixes, truncation flags, and monotonic started/completed timestamps.

Packages/macOS/CmuxRemoteWorkspace/Sources/CmuxRemoteWorkspace/Tunnel/RemoteDaemonProxySession.swift:369-371 closes only on remote EOF after forwarding its final payload

daemon_rpc.request_correlation: Each request receives a unique increasing id, is registered before the frame is written, and blocks its caller until the reader thread routes the response with the same id or the timeout expires.
daemon_rpc.stream_event_routing: Frames with ids resolve pending calls. Id-less proxy.stream.* frames route by exact stream_id to the subscribed receiver; unrelated stream ids and unrelated event families do not resolve calls or enter another stream.
daemon_rpc.thread_ownership: The caller of open/write/subscribe/close may block. A distinct transport reader must continue consuming and routing frames. Tests and production responders must therefore answer a synchronous request from another thread.
canonical_evidence: Packages/macOS/CmuxRemoteDaemon/Sources/CmuxRemoteDaemon/Client/RemoteDaemonRPCClient+RPC.swift:51-84 registers stream routing before synchronous subscribe
Packages/macOS/CmuxRemoteDaemon/Sources/CmuxRemoteDaemon/Client/RemoteDaemonRPCClient+RPC.swift:272-325 writes then blocks on a separately resolved pending call

daemon_stream_half_close_gap.finding: The daemon wire protocol exposes proxy.write, proxy.close, and stream data/eof/error, but no write-half-close RPC. Canonical local EOF deliberately keeps the remote stream open. Windows DaemonProxyStream currently maps Shutdown::Write to proxy.close, which is a full close and is not canonical-equivalent.
daemon_stream_half_close_gap.required_behavior: Shutdown::Write on a daemon-backed stream must not issue proxy.close. Shutdown::Both (or final terminal cleanup) must close once and unregister once. This preserves response draining after local EOF.

daemon_timeout_gap.finding: Windows currently uses DEFAULT_DAEMON_RPC_TIMEOUT (10 seconds) for stream writes and closes, while the frozen canonical contract uses 8 seconds for proxy.write and 4 seconds for proxy.close.
daemon_timeout_gap.required_behavior: Use operation-specific 8-second write and 4-second close deadlines so timeout and error timing match canonical behavior; connector/open timeout remains independently configurable.

reproduction.failure: proxy upstream relay failed: An established connection was aborted by the software in your host machine. (os error 10053)

reds.root_cause: After the in-memory remote returns immediate EOF, relay_bidirectional shuts down the server TcpStream write side and then read side before joining the upstream worker. On Windows, Shutdown::Read discards/aborts the peer's still-in-flight final bytes even though a cloned handle is reading them. The client write shutdown and/or the upstream read then observes WSAECONNABORTED (10053). Unix commonly tolerates this timing, hiding the ownership race.
minimal_fix: Do not call client.shutdown(Shutdown::Read) while the upstream worker may still read.
After downstream EOF, flush and half-close only client Write, join the upstream worker, then perform terminal read/full cleanup.
Make daemon-backed Shutdown::Write a non-closing half-close/no-op because proxy.close is full close; reserve close_once for Shutdown::Both/final cleanup.

reds.root_cause: This red is in test orchestration, not request correlation. The test calls stream.write_all on its sole coordinator thread. write_all synchronously sends request id 3 and waits up to 10 seconds. The same thread intends to call writer.wait_for_line(2) and send id 3's response only after write_all returns, so no responder can run and timeout is inevitable. Open and close already demonstrate the correct separate-thread pattern.
minimal_fix: Move stream.write_all(b"ping") to a worker thread and return the stream plus write result over a channel.
On the coordinator thread, observe request id 3, assert its method/stream/data, send the matching response, then join/receive the writer result before continuing.
Keep close on a worker thread and answer its exact request id from the coordinator thread.

test_first: Retain the existing relay test as a Windows race red and add a controlled barrier variant that proves upstream bytes are drained before read-side shutdown.
Correct only the RPC test scheduling first; its existing 10-second failure must become an immediate pass without changing production correlation code.
Add a daemon-stream half-close test asserting Shutdown::Write emits no proxy.close and later stream data/eof remains readable; Shutdown::Both emits exactly one proxy.close.
red_plan.simplification: Centralize direction completion/terminal cleanup ordering and express daemon close ownership through close_once; do not add sleeps, platform-specific error suppression, retry loops, or longer timeouts.

adversarial_acceptance: Relay test passes at least 1000 consecutive native Windows repetitions with zero 10053/10054 errors and exact upstream/downstream prefixes.
Barrier test delays upstream drain until downstream EOF and proves no local read shutdown occurs before drain completion.
Local client sends a request then Shutdown::Write; delayed remote response is still delivered completely before EOF.
Simultaneous EOF in both directions terminates without hang, duplicate observation, or duplicate close.
Daemon RPC test passes at least 250 consecutive repetitions and completes well below the 10-second request timeout.
Out-of-order responses for two concurrent request ids resolve only their matching callers.
An id-less stream event interleaved between request and response reaches only the exact stream subscription and does not consume the pending response.
Wrong-id, late-after-timeout, wrong-stream, malformed, EOF, and error frames do not deadlock or cross-route.
Shutdown::Write on DaemonProxyStream sends no proxy.close; terminal Shutdown::Both closes once, and subsequent drop only unregisters at most once.
Daemon proxy writes time out at 8 seconds and closes at 4 seconds, matching the frozen canonical RPC contract.
Full cmux-desktop native Windows test gate remains green after focused stress.
